entries.logic_thesis: Daoist doctrine is proven not by isolated revelation but by a hierarchical canon that maps ranks of texts to ranks of efficacy: higher scriptures govern deeper transformation because they encode more complete causal models of the Dao. The work establishes that orthodoxy is a logic of correspondence—name, rank, and function must cohere—so that misranked practice cannot yield true realization.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: Dao has graded manifestations; scriptures are vessels of those grades. 2) Inference: a text’s rank is its operational scope (cosmology, ethics, alchemy, ritual). 3) Therefore authority follows functional completeness, not mere antiquity. 4) Misapplication of a lower text to a higher aim is category error. 5) Conclusion: correct practice requires matching scripture class to the causal level of the problem.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Classify any BaZi or cultivation method by which layer it claims to move (qi, shen, ming, Dao). 2) Match method to a text class of equal scope before using it. 3) Reject “one chart, one fix” that ignores rank of cause. 4) When results fail, re-check category mismatch before blaming timing. 5) Build a personal hierarchy of techniques from coarse adjustment to fine attunement.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike encyclopedic catalogues that list titles only, 道典论 argues for a logic of ranking. It differs from pure ritual manuals by making classification itself the proof of orthodoxy, not procedural detail.

entries.logic_practice: 1) Establish fixed breath sessions aligned with daily stems/branches. 2) Reduce speech, anger, and excess sex as leakage control. 3) Use BaZi weak elements to time and color visualization of qi. 4) Track somatic markers (warmth, saliva, calm) as verification. 5) Progress only when baseline storage is stable.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 三十六水法 (external laboratory water methods), this is internal consumption of qi. Unlike moral precept texts, its proof is physiological: if the method is right, the body reports.

entries.logic_thesis: The Thirty-Six Water Methods prove that transformation of matter follows repeatable aqueous operations: dissolution, precipitation, decoction, and timed immersion are lawful stages, so “alchemy” is experimental chemistry guided by cosmological correspondences, not miracle alone.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: substances have fixed properties under water processes. 2) Named methods produce named products. 3) Cosmological timing modulates yield and purity. 4) Failure is method error or timing error, not mystery. 5) Conclusion: sacred pharmacy is protocol-driven causal science.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Respect sequence: prep → dissolve → transform → stabilize. 2) Map water operations metaphorically to chart “washing” of excess (e.g., strong fire cooled). 3) In practice (historical or modern herbal), control solvent, heat, and duration. 4) Document failures as parameter errors. 5) Do not confuse symbolic water with literal lab water without training.
entries.logic_compare: It differs from pure neidan (服內元炁) by externalizing process into vessels and reagents. It differs from later purely symbolic alchemy by preserving concrete laboratory logic.

entries.logic_thesis: The Heavenly Master’s oral secrets prove that written scripture is incomplete without master-keyed procedure: critical parameters (timing, proportion, taboo, visualization) travel in oral lineage because they are high-risk if misapplied. Transmission logic is security-through-person, not secrecy for prestige.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: advanced methods have narrow safe bands. 2) Writing under-specifies or over-discloses. 3) Oral instruction calibrates to student condition. 4) Lineage verifies both method and character. 5) Conclusion: true efficacy requires living transmission that completes the text.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Treat classic BaZi rules as partial; seek calibrated mentorship for edge cases. 2) Keep personal oral notes of what actually worked for which chart types. 3) Gate advanced breath/alchemy behind ethical readiness. 4) Prefer adaptive teaching over one fixed formula. 5) Verify lineage claims by result consistency, not titles alone.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike open encyclopedias (音义/科戒营始), this text’s argument is that openness without calibration is dangerous. Unlike purely popular 神仙传, it is procedural and teacher-centered.

entries.logic_thesis: The Yellow Court Dunjia Body-Affinity Scripture proves that internal landscape (Yellow Court) and strategic timing (Dunjia) cohere in the human body: escape from harm and attainment of longevity arise when spatial-energetic maps of the self align with temporal-strategic maps of heaven-earth. The body is both battlefield and sanctuary.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: body has hidden courts/gates; time has hidden doors (遁). 2) Affinity (緣身) means methods must attach to somatic loci. 3) Dunjia logic chooses when gates open. 4) Mis-timed or mis-sited practice fails. 5) Conclusion: integrated body-time strategy is the path of protection and refinement.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Locate practice in specific body centers (Yellow Court / dantian), not abstraction. 2) Choose hours/days using BaZi + Dunjia-like avoidance of clash. 3) In conflict years, emphasize concealment and conservation (遁) over aggressive expansion. 4) Combine visualization of inner court with calendar discipline. 5) Measure success by reduced crisis and clearer center.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike pure 黃庭 inner vision alone, it adds strategic time logic. Unlike pure 奇门遁甲 battlefield arts, it turns strategy inward onto the body.

entries.logic_thesis: The Taiqing Qi-Regulating Scripture proves that health and spiritual capacity are functions of rhythmic balance: qi must be tuned (調) like an instrument—neither forced nor neglected—through breath, posture, emotion, and seasonal matching. Disorder is detuning; cure is re-tuning.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: qi has tempo, direction, and density. 2) Excess/deficiency and counterflow create disease and agitation. 3) Regulation restores lawful circulation. 4) Season and constitution set the target tuning. 5) Conclusion: systematic 調氣 is the causal therapy of body-mind.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Diagnose BaZi for chronic excess/deficiency patterns. 2) Design breath ratios and movement to compensate. 3) Align sessions with seasonal qi (e.g., spring rising, autumn gathering). 4) Include emotional regulation as part of qi tuning. 5) Iterate weekly based on sleep, pulse feel, mood.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 服內元炁訣 (storage/ingestion focus), 調氣經 emphasizes dynamic balance. Compared with external 水法, it is wholly physiological and continuous.

entries.logic_thesis: The “behind-the-elbow” Jade Scripture Formulas prove that true medicine is portable emergency wisdom: the highest recipes are those usable at need, compact enough for the sleeve, selected by urgency and efficacy. Sacred healing is ranked by accessibility under constraint, not by esoteric length.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: crisis leaves no time for elaborate rites. 2) A few proven formulas cover critical cases. 3) Portability multiplies lives saved. 4) “Jade” marks verified quality, not ornament. 5) Conclusion: condensed, ready-to-hand methods embody the Dao of compassionate skill.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Build a personal “elbow bag” of BaZi first-aid rules for crisis years. 2) Prefer short, tested remedies over sprawling systems when time is short. 3) Pre-memorize 3–5 interventions (breath, diet, ritual, behavioral). 4) Document what worked in emergencies. 5) Teach family/students the portable subset first.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike vast 清微 or 法海 ritual corpora, this text’s logic is minimalism under pressure. Unlike hagiography, it is practical pharmacopeia ethics: what you can carry, you can use.

entries.logic_thesis: The Biographies of Immortals prove by narrative induction that immortality is a human-accessible trajectory: diverse persons, methods, and eras converge on transformation, so the Dao is not monopoly of one school. Case accumulation is the argument—multiplicity of paths under unity of attainment.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: many independent cases report similar outcomes. 2) Methods differ (herbs, breath, virtue, alchemy). 3) Shared result implies real possibility space. 4) Exemplars model virtues and errors. 5) Conclusion: immortality is demonstrated as a pattern of practice, not a single dogma.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Extract method types from stories and map to your BaZi constitution. 2) Imitate virtues (sincerity, perseverance) before exotic techniques. 3) Avoid literalism of miracle details; extract causal habits. 4) Use biographies as motivational evidence against fatalism. 5) Compare failed vs. successful conduct in the tales.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike systematic precept codes, 神仙传 argues by story. Unlike technical 口訣, it is public inspiration, not calibrated procedure—breadth over precision.

entries.name_han: 历世真仙体道通鉴续编
entries.logic_thesis: The Continuation of the Comprehensive Mirror of True Immortals proves that Daoist sanctity is historical and institutional: lineages, dates, and successive embodiments create a continuous evidence chain. Legitimacy flows from documented transmission across dynasties, not from isolated charisma.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: claims need historical continuity. 2) Biographies sequenced as a “mirror” allow comparison and audit. 3) Continuation updates the record as new saints appear. 4) Institutions preserve methods across deaths of individuals. 5) Conclusion: authentic Dao is a living historical series under critical collation.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Prefer techniques with traceable lineage notes. 2) Read lives as data: which practices correlated with which eras/conditions. 3) Update your own practice log as a personal “通鉴.” 4) Use historical caution against anachronistic mixing. 5) Balance innovation with documented roots.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with early 神仙传, the 通鉴续编 is more historiographic and Quanzhen-aware. Compared with pure doctrine (道典论), it proves by chronicle rather than by rank theory.

entries.name_han: 终南山说经台历代真仙碑记
entries.logic_thesis: The stele records of successive true immortals at Zhongnan’s Scripture Platform prove that sacred geography + institutional memory fix the Dao in place: a site of preaching becomes a durable ledger of realization. Stone inscription is the logic of permanence against oral loss.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: oral memory decays; place concentrates practice. 2) Steles name persons and virtues publicly. 3) Public record creates accountability and inspiration. 4) Continuity of site multiplies lineage force. 5) Conclusion: inscribed history at a holy mountain is proof architecture for the living tradition.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Anchor practice to a stable place/time (home altar as “说经台”). 2) Keep durable records of vows and breakthroughs. 3) Visit or visualize mountain lineage to reinforce commitment. 4) Use public commitment (teacher, community) as stele-like constraint. 5) Treat place-qi in BaZi (travel, residence) as part of cultivation design.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike portable biographies, this text’s argument is site-specific. Unlike abstract cosmology, it sacralizes a concrete mountain institution as the medium of truth.

entries.logic_thesis: The Precept Scripture of Lord Lao proves that cosmic order and personal liberation share one law: precepts are not arbitrary bans but the ethical geometry of the Dao. Breaking them multiplies disorder in self and world; keeping them aligns microcosm with the Way.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: Dao is orderly; humans can violate or mirror that order. 2) Precepts operationalize mirroring. 3) Violation generates karmic/energetic friction. 4) Observance clears friction and invites spiritual response. 5) Conclusion: moral law is metaphysical technology of harmony.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Adopt a minimal daily precept set (truth, non-harm, restraint). 2) Audit BaZi conflict years for ethical triggers (anger, greed). 3) Use confession/repair when broken, not denial. 4) Let precepts gate advanced techniques. 5) Measure progress by reduced internal conflict, not only luck events.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 初真戒, it speaks with Lord Lao’s cosmic authority and broader theological frame. Compared with ritual law codes, it is more foundational ethics than administrative regulation.

entries.logic_thesis: The Initial True Precepts prove that entry into the Dao requires a threshold filter: beginners must install basic restraints before advanced arts, because early chaos multiplies later error. First purity is a logical precondition of later “truth.”
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: beginners lack stable intention and body. 2) Simple clear rules stabilize both. 3) Without base restraint, advanced methods amplify defilement. 4) Ordination/commitment marks the threshold. 5) Conclusion: initial precepts are the causal foundation of all higher work.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Start cultivation with lifestyle hygiene (sleep, speech, diet, sex limits). 2) Delay complex BaZi magic or alchemy until base ethics hold. 3) Use checklist accountability for 30–100 days. 4) Revisit初真 when life chaos returns. 5) Teach newcomers precepts before chart gymnastics.
entries.logic_compare: It is narrower and more pedagogical than 九真明科’s multi-rank system. It differs from 老君戒经 by focusing on novitiate practicality rather than full theological breadth.

entries.name_han: 洞玄灵宝三洞奉道科戒营始
entries.logic_thesis: This Lingbao code proves that Daoist community is an engineered system: the Three Caverns, precepts, rituals, and institutional “营始” (founding/organization) must cohere so that collective practice produces reliable sacred order. Religion works when organization matches cosmology.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: individual practice is unstable without structure. 2) Three Caverns classify methods and ranks. 3) Precepts + rites regulate members. 4) Founding norms prevent entropy of the community. 5) Conclusion: institutional design is part of the Dao’s causal machinery.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Organize your practice like a small “abbey”: schedule, roles, rules. 2) Classify tools under clear categories (like 三洞). 3) Write house rules for family/altar discipline. 4) Use calendrical rites to synchronize members. 5) Review and re-found systems when chaos returns.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike solitary neidan manuals, this is socio-ritual engineering. Unlike pure biography collections, it legislates how a living order begins and runs.

entries.logic_thesis: The Qingwei Primordial-Descent Great Rites prove that high ritual efficacy descends from a primordial source through a pure (清微) lineage of thunder, talisman, and intentional method: power is not invented bottom-up but received and applied. Correct form channels 元降; wrong form blocks it.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: primordial qi/spirit can be invoked. 2) Lineage methods are calibrated receivers. 3) Talisman, mudra, breath, and decree align operator with source. 4) Moral purity maintains the channel. 5) Conclusion: great dharma is controlled descent of primordial force through pure protocol.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Approach advanced ritual only with purity prep and proper training. 2) Align petition with Qingwei domains (exorcism, weather, healing as taught). 3) Integrate BaZi timing for rite hours without inventing seals. 4) Treat intention-speech-action as one circuit. 5) Verify by ethical aftermath and reduced disorder, not spectacle.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 法海遗珠 (anthology of many methods), 清微 is a school-system with a unified metaphysics of descent. Compared with internal 調氣, it is more theurgic and command-oriented.

entries.logic_thesis: The Pearl Relics of the Dharma Sea prove that practical efficacy is often fragmentary: valuable methods survive as “pearls” scattered in a sea of rites, so the wise compiler preserves and selects working pieces rather than demanding one perfect system. Utility under diversity is the argument.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: living practice generates many local techniques. 2) Not all texts are complete systems. 3) Anthology saves rare effective modules. 4) User must select by case, not swallow whole. 5) Conclusion: the Dao’s working toolkit is modular; pearls matter more than ocean noise.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Extract single techniques from large corpora and test carefully. 2) Tag each “pearl” by problem type (haunt, illness, drought, luck). 3) Cross-check with ethics and BaZi suitability. 4) Prefer few proven pearls over hoarding. 5) Keep a personal 遗珠 notebook of results.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 清微’s unified school architecture, 法海遗珠 is eclectic and archival. Unlike 道典论’s ranking theory, it values practical remnants over pure hierarchical elegance.
